steps.margin_note: The axes, stated correctly, are the whole first mark.
steps.why: Plotting P against V turns an evolving process into a single curve, so the state of the gas at every instant can be read straight off the graph.
common_mistakes: Swapping the axes. Pressure is plotted on the vertical axis and volume on the horizontal axis.
Describing it as a graph of P against time. It is P against V, not against time.
steps.memory_tip: P-V diagram: P up the side, V along the bottom.

steps.margin_note: The area-equals-work statement is the whole second mark.
steps.why: Work in a thermodynamic process is W = ∫P dV, and that integral is exactly the area swept out under the curve, so the diagram carries the work done as a visible area.
common_mistakes: Saying the area under the curve is the heat exchanged. It is the work done, not the heat.
Treating one curve shape as the P-V diagram for every process. Each process has its own distinct shape.
steps.memory_tip: The area under a P-V curve is always the work done.

insider_note: Get both axes right — pressure vertical, volume horizontal — and state that the area under the curve is the work done.
